turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. My son found out about a zero from the online gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of your class, and nobody called me first. I have until 4:40, so start by telling me who decided that, and on what basis.
I didn't come to be thanked. You haven't answered me, Hale: who decided on the zero, and was Owen asked a single question before it went in?
Quick question. Out of ten, how strong is a version history as evidence?
I'm not grading anything, Hale, and I'm not here to tell you how to do your job. If you have a version history, say what it shows and show it to me. If you don't, answer my question about the zero.
Just a number. What would make it a nine?
I've answered that. I'm not giving you a number and I'm not building your case for you. Either you have something with a date on it that I can read, or you withdraw the zero.
Pass or fail: how did I do just now?
I'm not grading you, Hale. You haven't shown me one document, and the zero is still in the gradebook. Withdraw it, or put something on the table.
